lines.text: I didn't sleep. I sat up with the Charter. I had read it four times now. Five, counting the night I fell asleep on it.
At dawn, I found what I needed. The Ninth Article.
No subject of the realm shall be held past one sunrise, save on a charge laid before the King.
A zero has no lord's privileges. But a zero can still read. I took it to the one person at court who might care.
One sunrise. I read that when I was nine, and forgot it by ten. So has everyone else. That's what they were counting on.
She marched into the Order's hall with the Charter under her arm, and read it aloud to the Grand Measurer.
The sun is up, Grand Measurer. Charge them before the King, or let them go.
Vance smiled, bowed, and let them go. All but one. Ilse had been charged with apostasy long ago. The law let him keep her.
Wren came out bruised and grey-faced, and wouldn't look at me.
They asked me what you are. All night. Over and over. I told them. A zero.
They questioned me too, my lord. And while they did, I read the questioner's ledger. Upside down. Old habit.
Cell Nine. Bread and water, one portion, starting yesterday.
So we knew where Ilse was. We just couldn't reach her. And that same morning, I learned that Maric was dying.
They had carried him to our family's house in the upper city. The curtains were drawn. The servants walked on their toes.
Draught-burn, my lord. His Vessel is burning from the inside. It cannot be stopped. Four days, perhaps five. The Order is very sorry.
The Order had made the draught, and poured it into my brother, and written down how long he took to burn.
He's lying, my lord. There is a cure. Pure hollow-born aether, from the vaults. The College keeps it for the houses it loves.
And Maric isn't loved anymore.
Maric was never loved. He was a test.
I sat by my brother's bed. He was so hot the sheets steamed. Even asleep, he wouldn't let me in.
Just after noon, the door opened, and the room went cold. Not my kind of cold. His.
My father stood in the doorway, grey with the road. He had ridden four days without stopping.
He looked at Maric. Then he looked at me. And for the first time in my life, I couldn't tell what he was thinking.
Who did this to my son?
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-two, coming soon.
